title: Structs, references and const: an inventory
summary: Group data into your own types, find out the hard way that C++ copies by default, and learn when to pass by value, by reference and by const reference. Finish with std::optional and enum class.

steps.title: Your own type
hints: Declare `double total_value(const std::vector<Item>& items);` in the header, define it in inventory.cpp with a loop: `for (const Item& item : items) total += item.quantity * item.price;`

steps.title: The bug that copies

checks.label: restock takes the item by reference

hints: Set a breakpoint inside `restock` and step through the test. Watch `item.quantity` change… then step out and look at `nuts.quantity` in the test.
`item` is a *copy* of `nuts`. Change the parameter to `Item& item` — in both the header and the .cpp.

quiz.question: You're writing `print_item`, which only reads an Item to display it. Which parameter type is best?
explanations: It works, but it copies the whole Item — including its `std::string` — every time it's called, for no benefit.
No copy, but it tells every reader (and the compiler) that print_item might *change* the item. It also can't be called with a const Item or a temporary.
Yes: no copy, and the `const` is a compiler-checked promise not to modify it. This is the default for passing anything larger than a few numbers into a function that only reads it.
Pointers can be null, so the function would have to handle that case, and callers must write `&item`. Prefer references when "no object" isn't a valid input.

steps.title: Maybe there's an answer: std::optional
hints: Declare in inventory.h (and `#include <optional>`): `std::optional<std::size_t> find_index(const std::vector<Item>& items, const std::string& name);`
Return the index `i` when found (it converts to an optional automatically); after the loop, `return std::nullopt;`.

steps.title: Challenge: categories
hints: `enum class Category { Tool, Part, Consumable };` goes *above* `struct Item` (the struct uses it). Add `Category category = Category::Part;` as the struct's last member.
to_string: a `switch (category)` with one `case Category::Tool: return "tool";` per enumerator.
main: build the vector with four values per item, e.g. `{"wrench", 2, 12.0, Category::Tool}`, then loop and print.
